A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the X-ray background is dominated by the contribution of groups, and the microwave background is dominated by clusters.
the evolution in the hot gas properties is driven by evolution in the galaxy luminosity function and the two-point galaxy-galaxy correlation function.
the hot gas in groups and clusters is a significant source of fluctuations in the microwave and X-Ray backgrounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evolution of hot gas in galaxy clusters and groups is not a simple scaling of the local luminosities and temperature functions, but is a complicated function of the underlying dark matter and galaxy distributions.

the evolution of the luminosity function can be used to predict the evolution of the X-ray and CMB backgrounds and their fluctuations in a self-consistent manner, and that these predictions are in good agreement with the observations.
the X-ray background and the microwave background are both dominated by the hot gas in clusters and groups, not by individual galaxies.
